ClientResponses.Response:
Hey there. Thank you for reviewing our Pro 34 grill. We truly appreciate your feedback.

It sounds like you're experiencing temperature issues. The Pro 34 has a recommended closed lid start up. This means you would want to keep the lid closed and let your grill get to the desired or set temperature before putting your food down. When you set your grill to smoke, or any temperature setting, it will typically take 5-10 minutes to successfully ignite. Your grill will give off initial gray smoke, but once that goes away, you just want to let it get to the set temperature.

All newly purchased Traeger grills come with a 3-year warranty, so if you're experiencing these issues still, you're welcome to reach out to us for help. If you have any questions and/or concerns, please don't hesitate to reach out to us at 1-800-TRAEGER, and we'd be stoked to assist. We're here 7 days a week, 6am-10pm MST.

ClientResponses.Response:
Hey Chuck, Thank you for sharing your experience with your Pro 34. Maxing out at 370 is not a normal occurrence for these grills. 
 It is important to check the pellet quality. Good pellets should have a nice sheen to them, and you should hear a nice "snap" when breaking. A newly purchased or opened bag does not guarantee fresh pellets, especially if exposed to high humidity or moisture. 

Poor air circulation can play a role as well. Your Traeger relies on proper air circulation for the convection-style barrel to distribute the heat properly.
For grills with a chimney, try raising the cap up. Increasing the chimney height will cause more airflow, thus increasing the grill's temperature. 
Make sure items inside the grill are placed at least 1" from the sides of the grill.
Poor air circulation is often caused by drip tray liners/foil not being put on correctly, large pans, or too much food being placed too close to the edge of the grill.  

We would be stoked to do some troubleshooting with you to narrow down the cause of the low temp and get you back up and searing in no time.

I wasn't going to write this review, but it seems the only way to contact the company discreetly is by phone, so now I'm just going to go ahead and make this public. There is one important thing you should know about this particular model if you're planning to buy it.

Due to the design of the pellet feed auger assembly, there is a good possibility you will have to replace this part at-least once on this grill. The specific part number is "KIT0020" You can look that up and find it's general availability where you live. This auger drive motor and gear box is essentially free-floating off the end of the auger and due to this, it is very likely to get "bound up" destroying the small gears inside it's pot-metal gearbox. I'm not an engineer by trade but have taken a lot of things apart to fix them and this just blew my mind. Maybe this is a manufacturer defect and somebody forgot to install something on the assembly line but there are no detents or witness marks to indicate where a part should be installed or holes should be drilled etc. There is nothing holding the motor and gearbox in the proper place. It is allowed to turn around the auger shaft several degrees before the corner of the gearbox comes in contact with another metal fitment inside the housing. There's no little rubber stopper or anything there to indicate they intended the motor to be loose like this or anything else to indicate thought was put into building it this way.

This replacement part is not an expensive one, but you do have to take the entire feed pellet system apart and remove it from the grill to get to this motor. This means carefully removing wires and remembering where they go. Fortunately about half of them have the plugs marked with colored stickers that are *Almost* the same color so you can hope that's where that wire goes. It's just mains voltage so no biggie for a home gamer.

Having gone to several stores in my area to track down this elusive part 24 hours before I intend to cook a turkey in this grill, I have gotten a chance to see literally all of the other, newer versions of the auger feed system that Traeger has designed and put on the market. They are all much more sophisticated. Almost like entirely different engineers designed them.

If this was not a one off manufacturer defect, this grill needs to be recalled so the above design flaw can be fixed. This could also be remedied by designing a retrofit that owners of this model of grill could install to prevent the motor from being damaged. At no cost to the consumer.

If you still decide you want to get this model, at least now you know what to expect and what to look for.
